text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — streaming tail latency spike in eu-west2. p95 crossed 1.2s, p99 ~2.9s for streaming gateway. Autoscaling OK. Flagged: increased TLS handshake retries and NAT ephemeral port contention. https://incidents.internal/1719995000
oncall-sre: ack. I'm the IC. Paging netops + runtime-eng + infra-sre. Please post quick diffs/metrics.
netops: seeing a sudden bump in TLS handshake SYN-RETRANS and SYN-ACK RTTs from eu-west2-azb -> azc inter-AZ. DNS lookups also show elevated NXDOMAIN backoff on edge-proxies. NAT metrics show SNAT port utilization hit 85% on some subnets.
infra-sre: confirmed NAT ephemeral ports nearing exhaustion on a subset of private subnets (conntrack table growth). conntrack entries per node jumped ~3x in 10m.
runtime-eng: streaming runtime reports stalls at token emission stage; logs show repeated partial send failures and retry backoffs. sample log: ```[2024-04-12T14:12:03Z] stream_flush: write failed EPIPE, retry=3, backlog=12```
prod-support: inbound tickets from two key customers (ai-saas-co, docflow) about long streaming stalls and incomplete responses. CS flagged one as customer-facing outage.
customer-success: ai-saas-co on a support call, they're experiencing multiple 502s when streaming. They rely on eu-west2 for low-latency inference — this is high severity.
oncall-sre: quick mitigation checklist: 1) reduce traffic to affected AZ by shifting load 2) increase NAT port pool (if possible) 3) temporarily lower DNS TTL for edge-proxies 4) enable model fallback to sibling region for heavy customers. Which can we do ASAP?
netops: we can program route preference to steer new connections away from azb -> azc path within 2–3 mins using BGP route preference w/ SDN. Changing NAT config requires cloud console change (5–10m) and rolling restart of nat instances if using NAT instances. If using cloud-managed NAT, we can ask infra to increase ephemeral port allocation.
infra-sre: increasing cloud NAT port range now (submitted change). Also kicking conntrack cleanup on impacted nodes: `for n in $(nodes); do ssh $n sudo conntrack -F; done` — doing in 2 phases to avoid mass TCP drops. Will target 10% of nodes first.
runtime-eng: to reduce stalls we can lower per-stream buffer to avoid large backlog and increase keepalive freq to detect conn drops sooner. Pushing a hotfix config to edge proxies in 4–6m: `proxy.conf: stream_emit_batch=8 -> 4, keepalive=15s`
eng-ml: for high-value customers we can flip routing to eu-central fallback for their API keys. Need PM approval for emergency routing change and a small post-facto config change to preserve data locality (they accepted).
pm: Approved for emergency failover for named customers. PM will notify sales/CS.
oncall-sre: executing steps: 1) netops — please apply route preference to steer ~40% new traffic off azb->azc path (intent: immediate relief) 2) infra-sre — conntrack flush + cloud NAT increase 3) runtime-eng — push proxy config hotfix 4) eng-ml + prod-support — start targeted customer failovers.
netops: route change applied + verification: BGP metrics show decreased AS path usage on problematic link. New connection rates from edge proxies to azc dropped ~38% in 3m.
infra-sre: conntrack phased flush done on first cohort; cloud NAT port increase completed. Monitoring SNAT utilization — dropped from 85% -> 40% on impacted subnets.
runtime-eng: hotfix deployed to edge proxies in eu-west2-azb; stream buffer tuned. Early telemetry: streaming stall count down 60% in 8m. p95 now ~480ms, p99 ~1.1s (was p99 ~2.9s).
prod-support: CS reports ai-saas-co seeing improvement but still occasional spikes. They're keeping an eye on it.
customer-success: running a joint troubleshooting call with docflow, they're seeing timeouts reduced. :+1:
oncall-sre: marking incident as S0 -> mitigation in place. Still P1 until p99 < 700ms and no customer errors for 30m. Starting watch shift — @infra-sre take lead for next hour, @runtime-eng keep runtime telemetry, @netops monitor routes.
eng-ml: note for postmortem: evaluate reducing long-lived connection churn and review model shard placement: high fanout happened during a large gen job burst.
pm: prepping customer comms draft for affected tenants. cc @customer-success.
incident-bot: :bell: paging schedule: oncall-sre -> infra-sre (handoff) at 1719995400. Use channel #incidents for further updates.
infra-sre: taking handoff. Current state: NAT ports stable, conntrack baseline restored, route pref in place, runtime hotfix live. Still watching tail latency.
netops: continuing to watch TLS handshake retries — residual increase but trending down. DNS cache TTL lowered to 30s 10m ago; edge proxies honoring new TTLs.
oncall-sre: thanks team. We'll keep this thread for minute-by-minute updates. If anything spikes, escalate by paging + tagging critical customers. Postmortem owners: infra-sre + runtime-eng + netops.
eng-ml: flag: prepare canary to avoid mass fanout for multi-key jobs; would reduce connection bursts by ~30% in similar events.
prod-support: closing inbound tickets for now with note: monitoring.
infra-sre: 30m after mitigations: p95 320ms, p99 620ms, streaming error rate down to baseline. Moving to monitoring-only.
oncall-sre: incident moved to monitored-resolved state. Create postmortem and link here when ready. Great work — :phone: handoff complete.
